Source: http://www.drugsense.org/amma/

Posted August 11, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: The situation in California has become bizarre. In some parts of the state, San Francisco and Oakland, and other areas, mostly in Northern California, the medical marijuana situation is comparable to that in Vancouver, BC.

However, in other parts of the state, the situation is spinning out of control.

The state’s Attorney General is not enforcing the law, so rogue narks and prosecutors are aggressively violating not just Prop 215, but also basic Constitutional rights against warrantless searches and excessive bail.

See
Even In The State Capital, California Narks Violate Prop 215 and the Attorney General Won’t Do His Duty.
and
Selective Enforcement Versus Selective Compliance – 2 Articles
and
U.S. Bill of Rights

Attorney General Lockyer is required by the state’s constitution to enforce all the laws equally. Instead he is letting the narks run roughshod over some of the state’s most vulnerable citizens.
See
What Part Of 'Exempt' Do California District Attorneys Still Not Understand?

The marijuana resistance movement must demand that he do his duty. The late Peter McWilliams sued Lockyer’s predecessor, Dan Lungren, seeking his impeachment. The time has come to change the name on the papers to Lockyer and refile them.
See
Peter McWilliams Sues Lungren For Failing to Enforce Prop 215; Seeks His Impeachment

The narks are waging war not just on the sick and dying, but on the rule of law itself. Now is the time to fight back. I am going to spend the next week in California, reporting on the Kubby trial and the situation there.)

August 11, 2000
From The American Medical Marijuana Association
http://www.drugsense.org/amma/

$1/2 MILLION BAIL FOR 30 PLANTS - LOCKYER'S LEGACY

Bill Britt, a medical marijuana patient who is physically disabled and must use crutches, watched helplessly as Dave Zinc, the man who grows his medicine for him was arrested and jailed with $500,000 bail. Mr. Britt tried to persuade the police that they were in compliance with 11362.5, but the Long Beach police had instructions from the DA's office that, " the cultivation of Cannabis would not be allowed under ANY circumstances. "
See
Steve Kubby’s Interview With A Nark

Although only 30 plants were involved, police found equipment to make concentrated Cannabis " (Oil) which added " Manufacturing " to the charges of cultivation. Such equipment was allowed under Dan Lungren's original " Guidelines for Peace Officers, " which clearly states that concentrated forms of Cannabis are allowed by 11362.5. Nevertheless, the Long Beach District Attorney increased bail from $50,000 to $500,000.

Patients who use equipment to concentrate Cannabis do so for one purpose and that is to reduce what the government claims is a great threat of damage from smoking Cannabis. So because patients are attempting to protect themselves from what the Drug Czar claims are highly carcinogenic ingredients present in unprocessed marijuana, they must suffer even more as police add outrageous charges and bails.

Arresting and holding a patient for $1/2 million dollars is an obscenity. It shows how godless and traitorous law enforcement officials have become.
See
Lockyer Says He Will Not Fight For Or Against Medical Marijuana;
All That Is Necessary For the Triumph Of Evil Is For Enough Good AGs To Do Nothing
and
After Lockyer Says He Won’t Fight To Support Rights Under Prop 215
Former California Libertarian Party Gubernatorial Candidate And Medical Marijuana Patient
Steve Kubby Arrested On Cultivation And " Conspiracy " Charges!

We hold Attorney General Bill Lockyer personally responsible for this war on sick people, because he refuses to do his job and enforce the law equally and fairly throughout the state.

We patients have tried everything possible to get the police and prosecutors to uphold 11362.5. We've even gone to grand juries and filed complaints in several counties. Nevertheless, these blatant violations of the law and of human decency continue unopposed by the Attorney General.

It is time to hold Attorney General Bill Lockyer personally responsible for the horrible abuse and civil rights violations that he allows to go unchecked each day in the state of California.

When people say, " Prop. 215 is a bad law, " we're going to respond with, " No, Bill Lockyer is just a bad Attorney General who is afraid to stand up to the police. "

When the politicians ask us, " How can we fix 215, " we're going to tell them, " Impeach Bill Lockyer. "

When Bill Lockyer runs again for office and says, " I'm running on my record as Attorney General, " we will follow him like a bad smell and remind everyone that " Bill Lockyer aided and abetted a criminal war against sick and dying people, all for his own political gain. "

When Bill Lockyer reads this and says, " Forget 'em, they have no political power, " we will strengthen our resolve and swell our numbers, telling all that, " Bill Lockyer is the symbol of everything that this wrong with America today, because he refuses to uphold his oath of office or the Bill of Rights, while he hides behind police, and builds his reputation on the backs of sick, disabled and badly frightened people.

Attorney General Bill Lockyer may be a nice man and well-intentioned or he may secretly enjoy destroying the sickest and weakest members of society, we just don't know. We can only judge the man by his actions.

So long as the Attorney General allows such obvious and odious violations of the law to take place under his watch, he shows us by his actions that a war on sick people is preferable to facing off with rogue police and prosecutors, as is his job under the California Constitution.

THE AMERICAN MEDICAL MARIJUANA ASSOCIATION
